mainEntity.name: How much does a Jaguar XJ X358 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: Jaguar XJ X358 engine replacement costs range from £1,600 for a rebuilt 2.7 TDV6 diesel to £5,500 for a supercharged 4.2 V8. Supply-only rebuilt engines average £2,000-£5,500 depending on engine code, with supply-and-fit adding £800-£1,500 labour.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Jaguar XJ X358 V8?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning sign is a metallic rattle on cold start, lasting 1-3 seconds. As the tensioners worsen, the rattle may persist longer or occur on hot starts. Ignoring this warning risks the chain jumping teeth, causing valve-to-piston contact and catastrophic engine failure.

mainEntity.name: Is the Jaguar XJ X358 2.7 TDV6 diesel engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 2.7 TDV6 offers strong fuel economy and relaxed cruising but has a known vulnerability: crankshaft bearing failure that can snap the crankshaft. Regular oil changes (every 10,000 miles or annually) and prompt investigation of any bottom-end knock are essential to avoid catastrophic failure.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a high-mileage Jaguar XJ X358?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing an X358 engine is often worthwhile if the chassis, interior and electronics remain sound. With X358 values typically £3,000-£9,000, a rebuilt engine at £2,000-£5,500 can extend the car's life significantly. For cars valued under £4,000, a used engine may offer better value; above £6,000, a rebuilt unit with 12-month warranty is the smarter investment.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code fits my Jaguar XJ X358?

acceptedAnswer.text: Identify your X358 engine code by checking the VIN plate on the firewall, the service book, or using EnginesMarket's free registration lookup tool. X358 codes include AJ34 (4.2 V8 petrol), AJ33SC (4.2 supercharged V8), AJD/276DT (2.7 TDV6 diesel), RG (3.5 V8) and AJ-V6 (3.0 V6 petrol).

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the X350 and X358 Jaguar XJ?

acceptedAnswer.text: The X358 is the 2007 facelift of the X350, widely considered the last of the traditionally styled XJs. The X358 features a revised front grille and bumper assembly, side vents, rear tail lights and rear bumper. The engine range - 3.0 V6 petrol, 2.7 TDV6 diesel, 3.5 V8, 4.2 V8 and 4.2 supercharged V8 - remained unchanged.

historyTimeline.h2: Jaguar XJ X358 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Jaguar XJ X358 is the 2007 facelift of the third-generation X350, widely considered the last of the traditionally styled XJs. The X358 carried forward the X350's aluminium monocoque construction and six-speed ZF automatic transmission, with a revised front grille, bumper assembly, side vents and rear lights. Engine options spanned V6 petrol, V6 diesel and naturally aspirated or supercharged V8 units.

milestones.description: X350 launch: 3.0 V6 petrol (AJ-V6), 3.5 V8 (RG), 4.2 V8 (AJ34), 4.2 supercharged V8 (AJ33SC)
2.7 TDV6 diesel (AJD) introduced for UK/European markets
X358 facelift: revised styling, same engine range continues
End of X358 production (83,556 X350/X358 units produced total)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Jaguar XJ X358 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Jaguar XJ X358 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Jaguar XJ X358 is a precision-engineered luxury saloon, but its engines have well-documented vulnerabilities. The 2.7 TDV6 diesel (AJD) is prone to catastrophic crankshaft bearing failure, while the AJ34 and AJ33SC V8 petrol units suffer from timing chain tensioner wear as mileage accumulates. Every rebuilt X358 engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded internal components designed to address these original failure points, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Use the breakdowns below to compare repair costs against full replacement.

problems.h4: 2.7 TDV6 Crankshaft Bearing Failure - Why the Jaguar XJ X358 Diesel Engine Can Fail Catastrophically
problems.rootCause: The engine can spin its main bearings, starving the engine of oil - in extreme cases the crankshaft can actually snap. This is often linked to oil pump housing failure or inadequate oil pressure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Engine strip-down, crankshaft replacement, bearing replacement, oil pump inspection
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if caught early before extensive damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of remanufactured AJD unit with upgraded internals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended once crankshaft damage is confirmed

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Jaguar XJ X358 currently sits in the £3,000-£9,000 value band depending on condition, mileage and trim. With a full rebuilt engine costing £4,000-£5,800, replacement represents 45-80% of vehicle value. For X358s valued under £4,000, a used engine may be the more economical route; for cars above £6,000, a rebuilt unit with warranty offers stronger long-term value.
problems.recommendation: If your X358 2.7 TDV6 has developed a knocking noise from the bottom end, stop driving immediately and have the oil pressure tested. If crankshaft damage is confirmed, a used engine from a verified donor is the cheapest option, but a rebuilt unit with upgraded internals and 12-month warranty provides better peace of mind. Given the labour intensity of in-situ repairs, full replacement is often the most cost-effective route once bearing failure has occurred.

problems.h4: 4.2 V8 Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why AJ34 & AJ33SC X358 Engines Develop Cold-Start Rattle
problems.affectedModels: Jaguar XJ X358 4.2 V8 (AJ34) and 4.2 Supercharged V8 (AJ33SC, 2003-2009)
problems.rootCause: Early Jaguar V8 timing chain tensioners were plastic and subject to premature wear. Left unchecked, the timing chains could jump teeth, leading to catastrophic valve-to-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacing chains, guides and tensioners with upgraded metal-design components
repairOptions.longevity: 100,000+ miles if completed before stretch; strictly preventative

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of fully rebuilt unit with upgraded tensioners, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required once chain has jumped or valves have contacted pistons

problems.vehicleValueCheck: With X358 values ranging from £3,000-£9,000, a preventative chain kit at specialist prices (£1,600-£2,100) represents a sound investment if caught early. Full engine replacement (£4,200-£6,500) makes sense on cars valued above £6,000, but on sub-£4,000 examples, evaluating scrap value before committing is strongly advised.
problems.recommendation: On any X358 V8 exceeding 60,000 miles with an unknown service history, we strongly recommend having the cam covers removed to inspect the condition of the tensioners and chains. If cold-start rattle is already present, do not continue driving - book an inspection immediately. A preventative chain kit is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement and, with upgraded metal tensioners, provides a permanent fix.
